brief: UBS sales-desk roundup across two conferences. At the European Conference, growth is narrow: concentrated in structural-capex sectors (grid, electrification, data centers, defence, energy infrastructure, industrial automation, mining) with tight supply to 2028/29, while broader demand is absent, pushing non-growth companies toward cost cuts, capacity rationalization and M&A, with proceeds going to shareholders, not debt repair. Investors were cautious, not capitulating: two-thirds expect government debt to end in monetisation, 88% see French spreads as not yet peaked, yet a majority stayed bullish on US equities. UBS's base case is muddle-through, not resolution, with France the likely next test. At the Australasia Conference, RBA/RBNZ speakers were hawkish as AI buildout feeds inflation concerns with little productivity offset so far, though AI speakers were more upbeat on productivity gains later this decade; Australian earnings forecasts are falling at the fastest pace since Covid. Separately, hedge fund gross-exposure volatility is at record highs even as index vol falls, leaving elevated shorts that could fuel an unloved year-end rally. Hot, broad-based US CPI repriced the Fed hiking path higher and lifted the dollar, with Jefferson now the Fed voice to watch over Warsh. More data-center scrutiny could raise, not cut, AI power spending.
